unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Nachman hears people slandering the Besht, grows angry and answers them with a parable, so there is a framing event as well as a mashal.

stories.end_quote: האיך אתם יכולים להכניס ראשכם בזה
stories.summary_en: R. Nachman, angered by people speaking ill of the Besht, tells them a parable: two ministers argue over how to set a jewel in the king's crown, both for the king's honour, and they rebuke a commoner who meddles. Disputes among the great are an ancient matter, like those between Saul and David or Hillel and Shammai, and outsiders should not intrude.

tags.why: The core of the story is a mashal told by the tzaddik.

quotes: והיטב חרה לו עד מאוד עבור זה
tags.why: R. Nachman is angered by the slander.

quotes: מאנשים שהיו מדברים סרה על הבעש"ט
tags.why: People speak against the Besht, and the theme is disputes among the great.

quotes: וכן ג"כ מחלוקת שבינינו היא מחלוקת ישינה
tags.why: Implies a dispute between tzaddikim (apparently involving the Besht) that outsiders must not judge.

quotes: הלא אנחנו יודעים גדולת המלך מאד
tags.why: Only tzaddikim understand their own disputes; ordinary people may not judge them.

quotes: מאנשים שהיו מדברים סרה על הבעש"ט
tags.why: The slanderers may be opponents or outsiders.
A didactic answer in the form of a mashal.
